title: Tutte’s 5-flow conjecture
formal: Does every finite loopless bridgeless undirected multigraph G admit an orientation of every edge and an assignment \(f:E(G)\to \{1,2,3,4\}\) such that, at each vertex, the sum of f on incoming edges equals the sum on outgoing edges as integers?
definitions: A finite loopless undirected multigraph consists of a finite vertex set and a finite set of distinct edge identities, each with two different endpoints. Several edges may have the same endpoint pair. An edge is a bridge if deleting that edge increases the number of connected components. Bridgeless means there are no such edges; disconnected graphs and isolated vertices are allowed. An orientation chooses a tail and head for each edge independently. At vertex v, integer flow conservation is \(\Sigma\)_{\(e:head(e)=v\)}\(f(e)=\Sigma\)_{\(e:tail(e)=v\)}\(f(e)\), with empty sums zero. A nowhere-zero k-flow is such an orientation and assignment with values \(1,\ldots ,k- 1\). The statement is an existence assertion, not a bound on construction time, and does not impose an embedding or a vertex-degree bound.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Determine whether four nonzero integral flow values suffice for every graph with the necessary bridgelessness condition.

importance.reason: A defining flow-existence conjecture with consequences for graph decompositions, orientations and directed-cut packing.

references.title: Approximately Packing Dijoins via Nowhere-Zero Flows
references.authors: Gérard Cornuéjols; Siyue Liu; R. Ravi
references.locator: Conjecture 3; definition of integral nowhere-zero flows and connection with dijoin packing

progress.text: Seymour’s 6-flow theorem gives the corresponding universal result with values 1 through 5, as recalled in the cited paper.
Cornuéjols, Liu and Ravi state the 5-flow conjecture and connect nowhere-zero flow bounds to approximate dijoin packing.

context_blocks.text: A nowhere-zero flow circulates a nonzero amount through every edge without accumulating anything at a vertex. Bridges prevent such circulation, so bridgelessness is a necessary condition.

The established 6-flow theorem proves that five positive integer values suffice. Tutte asks whether the palette can always be reduced to four. The orientation is part of the witness, so negative values in a fixed orientation are represented by reversing edges.

The 2025 work exhibits a quantitative connection between flow existence and disjoint sets meeting directed cuts. This gives the conjecture an algorithmic and optimization role beyond the existence of an edge labeling.

sentences: Tutte’s conjecture asks for a nowhere-zero 5-flow in every bridgeless graph.
Each edge receives a direction and an integer from one to four.
At every vertex the incoming and outgoing totals must agree.
Parallel edges are allowed and are treated as distinct edges.
The claim would sharpen the universal 6-flow theorem and strengthen a central graph-decomposition principle.

status_note: Reviewed through 11 September 2026. The 2025 paper explicitly states the general 5-flow conjecture; the same-day search found no resolution. The known 6-flow theorem does not settle the target.

notes: Fixed integer rather than merely modular conservation, allowed parallel edges, and stated the bridge condition componentwise.
